Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

Do not imply that the older policy information has been revalidated for 2028.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Cherrywood Renter’s-Insurance Claims-Intake Worksheet — 2028", "folder": "Cherrywood", "body": "CHERRYWOOD RENTER’S-INSURANCE CLAIMS-INTAKE WORKSHEET
Household use | Prepared January 1, 2028

IMPORTANT — VERIFY BEFORE RELYING ON FIGURES
This is an intake aid for organizing facts and questions. It is not a coverage determination, claim decision, legal advice, or a substitute for the policy, endorsements, exclusions, or insurer/adjuster instructions.

The figures below are the latest documented Cherrywood policy information available in our records, from the renewal effective May 1, 2027. They have NOT been revalidated for 2028. Before relying on any limit, deductible, effective date, interested-party listing, or other term, obtain and verify the latest 2028 declarations page and policy documents. If the latest declarations page differs, use the latest insurer-issued documents and ask the insurer how the difference applies.

HOUSEHOLD AND POLICY IDENTIFICATION

Household members / occupants to identify on the claim
- Riley Tanaka — policyholder/household member: ______________________________
- Sam — household member: _________________________________________________
- Kibo — household dog/pet; not assumed to be a named insured: ______________
- Other occupant(s), resident(s), or affected person(s): ______________________

Policy details to complete from the latest declarations page
- Insurer: ________________________________________________________________
- Policy number: _________________________________________________________
- Named insured(s) exactly as shown: _______________________________________
- Property/risk address: Cherrywood, exact address: _________________________
- Current policy effective date: __________________  Expiration date: _______
- Claim date and approximate time: _________________________________________
- Date reported to insurer: ________________________________________________
- Claims representative / phone / claim number: _____________________________

Interested party
- Documented interested party: Cherrywood
- Verify on the latest declarations page that Cherrywood is still listed and copy the exact legal name/address here:
  ________________________________________________________________________

DOCUMENTED POLICY SNAPSHOT — NOT REVALIDATED FOR 2028
These are reference fields only; confirm each one against the latest declarations page before using them.
- Most recently documented effective date: May 1, 2027
- Most recently documented annual premium: $318.00
- Personal property: $30,000, replacement-cost basis
- Personal liability: $300,000
- Documented deductible: $500; confirm which coverage(s) it applies to and whether any separate deductible exists
- Loss of use / additional living expense: $10,000
- Water-backup coverage: $5,000; confirm sublimit, trigger, deductible, and exclusions
- Other limits, sublimits, endorsements, exclusions, or scheduled items: __________

CLAIM INTAKE — COMPLETE FOR EVERY SCENARIO
- Scenario(s): [ ] Property loss  [ ] Liability  [ ] Temporary displacement  [ ] Water backup
- What happened, in plain language: _________________________________________
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Date, time, and location: ________________________________________________
- Who discovered or witnessed it? _________________________________________
- Is anyone injured or in immediate danger? [ ] No  [ ] Yes — emergency action/contact:
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Steps taken to prevent further damage (only if safe): ______________________
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Emergency services, police, fire, plumber, restoration company, or landlord contacted:
  Who/date/reference: _____________________________________________________
- Photos/video taken before cleanup or disposal? [ ] No  [ ] Yes, stored at: __
- Evidence preserved, including damaged items and receipts? [ ] No  [ ] Yes
- Has the insurer been notified? [ ] No  [ ] Yes — date/method: _____________
- Do not admit fault, promise payment, discard damaged property, or authorize major permanent repairs without following the policy/insurer’s instructions, except reasonable emergency measures to protect people and prevent additional damage.

SCENARIO 1 — PROPERTY LOSS
Use for theft, fire, smoke, storm, vandalism, accidental damage, or other loss/damage to personal property.

Event and property
- Cause/peril suspected (do not treat this as a coverage conclusion): __________
- Residence area or off-premises location: __________________________________
- Security/police report number, if applicable: ______________________________
- Item description, make/model, serial number, age/date acquired, and owner:
  ________________________________________________________________________
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Quantity and condition before loss: ______________________________________
- Replacement estimate or current price: $__________________________________
- Purchase receipt, appraisal, photo, warranty, or other proof available? ______
- Was the item used for ordinary personal/remote work, personal transportation, hobby, or business inventory? __________________________________________
- Was any item scheduled or individually listed? ____________________________
- Was the loss away from the residence? ____________________________________

Property-loss reference questions
- Confirm whether the $30,000 personal-property limit and replacement-cost treatment shown above are current.
- Ask whether the documented $500 deductible applies, and whether a separate deductible, category sublimit, endorsement, or exclusion applies.
- Ask what documentation is required and whether payment may begin at actual cash value with recoverable depreciation paid after replacement and receipts.
- Confirm any special limits for electronics, bicycles, art supplies, jewelry, cash, business property, or property away from the residence.

Itemization attachment: Add rows or attach a separate inventory.
Item | Owner | Description/serial | Date acquired | Amount claimed | Proof attached | Notes
1. _______________________________________________________________________
2. _______________________________________________________________________
3. _______________________________________________________________________
4. _______________________________________________________________________

SCENARIO 2 — LIABILITY
Use when a household member may be legally responsible for bodily injury, property damage, or related expenses claimed by another person.

People and allegations
- Injured or affected third party: _________________________________________
- Contact information: ___________________________________________________
- What does the person say happened? ______________________________________
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Date, time, location, and witnesses: _____________________________________
- Injury or damage described (without admitting responsibility): _____________
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Demand, invoice, letter, citation, lawsuit, or other notice received? [ ] No [ ] Yes
  Date received and attach/copy details: ___________________________________
- Any insurer, attorney, property manager, medical provider, or agency already contacted?
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Potentially involved household member, guest, pet, or property: ____________

Liability reference questions
- Confirm whether the $300,000 personal-liability limit is current and what coverage grant applies.
- Ask whether a deductible applies to this liability matter; do not assume the documented $500 property deductible applies.
- Notify the insurer promptly and provide every demand, summons, letter, photograph, and witness detail. Do not admit fault or agree to a settlement without insurer direction.
- If a lawsuit or formal deadline exists, record the deadline and seek prompt legal/insurer guidance:
  ________________________________________________________________________

SCENARIO 3 — TEMPORARY DISPLACEMENT
Use when a covered event may make the residence unfit to live in or requires temporary relocation.

Habitability and displacement
- Why is the residence unsafe, inaccessible, or uninhabitable? ________________
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Who cannot remain there? _________________________________________________
- Date/time the residence was vacated or may need to be vacated: ____________
- Landlord/property manager notified? [ ] No [ ] Yes — date/contact: _________
- Government, fire department, restoration company, or other determination of habitability:
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Temporary lodging address and dates: _____________________________________
- Household members and pet needing placement: _____________________________
- Accessibility, work, school, medication, transportation, or other constraints:
  ________________________________________________________________________

Expense log
Date | Expense/vendor | Category | Amount | Receipt attached | Insurer approval/reference
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________

Loss-of-use reference questions
- Confirm whether the $10,000 loss-of-use/additional-living-expense limit is current, what expenses qualify, and whether it is a limit, time cap, or subject to other restrictions.
- Ask whether lodging, increased food cost, pet charges, transportation, storage, laundry, and other expenses are eligible, and what documentation or preapproval is required.
- Do not assume displacement is covered merely because the residence is inconvenient; ask the insurer about the covered event and habitability standard.

SCENARIO 4 — WATER BACKUP
Use for water or wastewater backing up through drains, sump systems, or similar points. If the source is a burst pipe, appliance leak, roof leak, flooding, or another event, describe that separately and ask the insurer which coverage applies.

Source and immediate response
- Suspected source/entry point: _____________________________________________
- Water type (clean, contaminated, sewage, unknown): ________________________
- Area(s) affected and approximate depth/extent: ____________________________
- Date/time discovered and whether flow continues: __________________________
- Shutoff, extraction, drying, or emergency mitigation performed: ____________
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Plumber/restoration vendor, invoice, photos, moisture report, or report number:
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Any mold, structural, electrical, flooring, furniture, electronics, or personal-property damage?
  ________________________________________________________________________
- Is the property safe to enter? [ ] Yes  [ ] No — instructions/contact: ______

Water-backup reference questions
- Confirm that water-backup coverage is present on the latest declarations page and whether the documented $5,000 amount is current.
- Ask whether $5,000 is per occurrence, an aggregate, or subject to another sublimit; ask whether cleanup, tear-out, drying, mold, contents, and additional living expenses are included or separately limited.
- Confirm the applicable deductible, including whether the documented $500 deductible applies or a separate water-backup deductible applies.
- Ask about exclusions and whether the described source is water backup, plumbing leakage, flood, groundwater, seepage, appliance leakage, or another category.
- Preserve damaged materials and belongings when safe; photograph before disposal and follow the insurer/restoration instructions.

Water-damage inventory / costs
Item or area | Damage | Emergency action | Estimate/invoice | Photo/report attached | Notes
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________

DOCUMENTS AND FOLLOW-UP CHECKLIST
- [ ] Latest 2028 declarations page obtained and all limits/deductibles verified
- [ ] Full policy and endorsements reviewed or insurer asked for applicable provisions
- [ ] Claim number and adjuster contact recorded
- [ ] Photos/video and incident timeline saved
- [ ] Police/fire/plumber/restoration reports saved
- [ ] Receipts, estimates, invoices, inventories, and proof of ownership saved
- [ ] Communications log maintained (date, person, method, summary)
- [ ] Temporary lodging and additional expenses tracked separately
- [ ] Landlord/property manager notified as appropriate
- [ ] Deadlines, inspections, proof-of-loss requests, and mitigation instructions recorded

COMMUNICATION LOG
Date/time | Person/company | Method | Subject | Action or document promised | Follow-up date
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________
___________________________________________________________________________

FINAL REMINDER
This worksheet records reported facts and questions; it does not determine whether a loss is covered or how much will be paid.
